title: Parallax
description: Parallax cinematography is the relative apparent motion between near and far objects as the camera translates. Near things race, far things crawl; that speed difference is how the image proves the world has layers.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: Prove the world has layers. A foreground railing, a mid-ground person, a far ridge: once the camera moves, their relative speeds cannot be faked by a zoom.
The shot is less a named rig than a test you apply to any travel. A zoom that claims depth will fail this test.
If you need a graphic flatten, zoom on purpose. If you need air and furniture, translate.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Any real translation works: dolly, tracking, arc, handheld, aerial. Place a near object in frame (post, glass, leaves).
The near plane should slide faster than the subject, the subject faster than the horizon. Prompt: Parallax around [Subject], near things racing, far things crawling, depth proven by relative speed.

sections.title: When to use it

blocks.text: Use it when the room or land must feel thick: a walk past columns, a car past trees. Do not add fake 2.5D wobble to a still and call it a dolly.

sections.title: Compared with similar shots

blocks.text: A Dolly is a wheeled translation that produces parallax. Tracking Shot produces it along a path.
A Zoom changes size without relative speed between planes. A Wiggle is a tiny stereo rock, parallax as a fidget, not a path.

sections.title: In film

blocks.text: The Tree of Life uses moving viewpoints so near nature shears against far sky. Gravity lets debris and faces disagree in speed as the camera translates.
Grammar: relative motion as proof of depth.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: The usual wrong cousin is a zoom. The tell: the whole picture enlarges as one card.
The fix: translate the camera and keep a near object in frame so it outruns the horizon.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is Parallax in film?
Parallax is the relative apparent motion of near and far objects when the camera translates. Near planes slide faster; that difference proves depth.
Parallax vs Zoom
A zoom scales the image from a locked body, so planes do not shear. Parallax needs the camera to move through space.
When should I use Parallax?
Use it whenever travel should prove a thick world: columns, glass, trees. Do not fake it with a zoom.
How do I prompt Parallax for AI image or video?
Write a translating camera and a near object that slides faster than the far plane. Example: Parallax around [Subject], near things racing, far things crawling, depth proven by relative speed.
